shot.purpose: Turn the first fix into visible proof that Sunny is making the party wetter and less free.
shot.performanceAssignment: Performance phases: anticipation: ENVIRONMENT The soaked garland sags against the cave wall; drops gather, fall, and mark the floor beneath it; action: Sunny Sunny’s paws tense, then release the garland; it falls flat and pushes muddy water outward onto Keen’s toes; reaction: Keen Keen looks down, wiggles his toes in the new puddle and gives one happy stomp that sends a small splash up; settle: Sunny Sunny recoils from the splash area, face tightening as she stands between wet ribbons and the fallen garland. Cause and effect: Water weight makes the garland sag and drip; Sunny’s release turns the overhead drip into a floor impact; the impact spreads muddy water to Keen; Keen’s stomp proves the puddle can become play; Sunny’s recoil stops that possibility. Visible turn: The room briefly opens into fun through Keen, then narrows again when Sunny treats the same water as a threat to her plan. Land on: The fallen garland, active muddy puddle, stalled Keen and tightened Sunny must all remain visible as the handoff to her next rush. Acting freedom: Let the drip rhythm, splash height and Keen’s toe wiggle vary, but preserve the cause chain from sag to drop to splash to Sunny’s recoil.
